channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: Africa’s largest private defence company moves to supply Ukraine with new armoured vehicle
item.description: South Africa-based defence and aerospace manufacturer Paramount Group is seeking to establish a presence in Ukraine’s rapidly expanding armoured vehicle market, signalling Africa’s growing role in global defence supply chains even as Pretoria maintains complex diplomatic ties with Russia.

item.title: Ghana limits foreign investments by local funds to support cedi, boost economic stability
item.description: Ghana’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has ordered local fund managers to scale back offshore investments as part of efforts to support the cedi and bolster macroeconomic stability.

item.title: Ghana recalls High Commissioner to Nigeria in rare governance move
item.description: President John Dramani Mahama has directed the immediate recall of Mohammed Baba Jamal Ahmed, popularly known as Baba Jamal, from his position as Ghana’s High Commissioner to the Federal Republic of Nigeria, following allegations of voter inducement during the National Democratic Congress (NDC) parliamentary primaries in the Ayawaso East Constituency.

item.title: South Africa to pull its troops from UN peacekeeping mission in Congo after 27 years
item.description: South Africa will withdraw its troops from the United Nations peacekeeping mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo as the continent’s largest economy seeks to realign the resources of its armed forces.

item.title: Epstein wanted to set up a financial system in one of Africa’s most ‘broken’ economies
item.description: The American financier, Jeffrey Epstein, who later became the central figure of an intricate criminal network involving sex trafficking, almost invested in Zimbabwe's economy, which in recent years has recorded tremendous recovery.

item.title: Namibia says it was unaware of high stakes TotalEnergies and Petrobras offshore deal
item.description: Namibia’s government said it was not notified of the planned acquisition by TotalEnergies and Brazil’s Petrobras of stakes in an offshore exploration licence, raising questions over whether the transaction will proceed.

item.title: U.S., China and India compete for Congo cobalt firm owned by Kenyan-Indian multimillionaire Shiraz Virji
item.description: U.S., Chinese and Indian investors are competing for cobalt assets in the Democratic Republic of Congo, targeting Chemaf, a Virji family-controlled miner, as Africa emerges as a strategic battleground for minerals critical to future technologies.

item.title: Angola seeks to purchase a 20%-30% strategic stake in world’s leading diamond company
item.description: Angola is seeking to acquire a 20%–30% stake in De Beers, the diamond unit being put up for sale by Anglo American, as part of a proposal being discussed with other African diamond-producing nations.

item.title: The US has adopted a new strategy against China in its battle for Africa’s critical minerals
item.description: The United States’ and China’s brawl for African resources such as copper, cobalt and other critical minerals has led the United States to leverage offtake deals and state-backed funding in order to remain competitive.

item.title: Top 10 African countries with the most access to foreign exchange right now
item.description: As African countries stare down the barrel of potentially tougher global financial conditions in 2026, access to foreign exchange (FX), especially considering the debacle of the gold market, presents a very interesting challenge.
